text: Ireland achieved impressive growth in 2025, driven primarily by MNE sector exports and investment recovery. Real GDP growth stood at 12.3 percent, with value added in MNE-dominated sectors rising by 25 percent compared to less than 1 percent in domestic sectors. Real goods exports grew 23 percent, driven by pharmaceutical shipments, pushing the US share of merchandise exports to 43 percent. This structure highlights the exposure of aggregate trade, growth, and tax outcomes to firm-specific and policy-driven shocks, reaffirming the need for adjustments for MNE activities when assessing Ireland’s external position.
